literal: Vanguard having-withstood that-which-advances [is] army, upon that-came battle withstanding capability having-known.
translation: A true army is one that knows its capacity to withstand the battle that has come upon it, and advances by breaking through the enemy's vanguard.
modern: தன் மேல் வந்த போரைத் தாங்கும் ஆற்றலை அறிந்து, பகைவரின் முன்னணிப் படையைத் தடுத்து முன்னேறிச் செல்வதே சிறந்த படையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the core strength of a capable army. The word 'தார்' can mean a garland, but in this military context, it specifically refers to the vanguard or the front line of the opposing force. A true army first understands its own capability ('தன்மை') to endure the battle that is forced upon it. With this tactical awareness, it successfully withstands the enemy's initial charge and continues to advance.
